arxiv-2011-04060.title: Closed-form Tight Bounds and Approximations for the Median of a Gamma Distribution
arxiv-2011-04060.creator: Richard F. Lyon
arxiv-2011-04060.description: Abstract We show how to find upper and lower bounds to the median of a gamma distribution, over the entire range of shape parameter k > 0 k>0 , that are the tightest possible bounds of the form 2 − 1 / k ( A + B k ) 2^{-1/k}(A+Bk) , with closed-form parameters A A and B B .

arxiv-2101-07650.title: On Fuzzification of n n -Lie Algebras
arxiv-2101-07650.creator: Shadi Shaqaqha
arxiv-2101-07650.description: Abstract . The aim of this paper is to introduce the notion of intuitionistic fuzzy Lie subalgebras and intutionistic fuzzy Lie ideals of n n -Lie algebras. It is a generalization of intuitionistic fuzzy Lie algebras. Then, we investigate some of characteristics of intutionistic fuzzy Lie ideals (resp. subalgebras) of n n -Lie algeras.

arxiv-2105-04660.title: Deletion to Scattered Graph Classes I - case of finite number of graph classes Preliminary version of the paper appeared in proceedings of IPEC 2020
arxiv-2105-04660.creator: Ashwin Jacob, Jari J. H. de Kroon, Diptapriyo Majumdar, Venkatesh Raman
arxiv-2105-04660.description: Abstract Graph-modification problems, where we modify a graph by adding or deleting vertices or edges or contracting edges to obtain a graph in a simpler class, is a well-studied optimization problem in all algorithmic paradigms including classical, approximation and parameterized complexity.

arxiv-2107-08374.title: Detecting Braess Routes: an Algorithm Accounting for Queuing Delays With an Extended Graph Thanks: This project was sponsored in part by the joint NSF-DOT CPS grant CNS-1545116 - Traffic Operating System for Smart Cities.
arxiv-2107-08374.creator: Mikhail Burov, Can Kizilkale, Alexander Kurzhanskiy, Murat Arcak
arxiv-2107-08374.description: Abstract The Braess paradox is a counter-intuitive phenomenon whereby adding roads to a network results in higher travel time at equilibrium. In this paper we present an algorithm to detect the occurrence of this paradox in real-world networks with the help of an improved graph representation accounting for queues.

arxiv-2108-05275.title: A General Cardinality Estimation Framework for Subgraph Matching in Property Graphs
arxiv-2108-05275.creator: Wilco van Leeuwen, George Fletcher, Nikolay Yakovets
arxiv-2108-05275.description: Abstract Many techniques have been developed for the cardinality estimation problem in data management systems. In this document, we introduce a framework for cardinality estimation of query patterns over property graph databases, which makes it possible to analyze, compare and combine different cardinality estimation approaches.

arxiv-2202-05955.title: Random primes in arithmetic progressions
arxiv-2202-05955.creator: Pascal Giorgi, Bruno Grenet, Armelle Perret du Cray, Daniel S. Roche
arxiv-2202-05955.description: Abstract We describe a straightforward method to generate a random prime q q such that the multiplicative group 𝔽 q ∗ \mathbb{F}_{q}^{*} also has a random large prime-order subgroup. The described algorithm also yields this order p p as well as a p p ’th primitive root of unity ω \omega .

arxiv-2207-09150.title: On the Usability of Transformers-based models for a French Question-Answering task
arxiv-2207-09150.creator: Oralie Cattan, Christophe Servan, Sophie Rosset
arxiv-2207-09150.description: Abstract For many tasks, state-of-the-art results have been achieved with Transformer-based architectures, resulting in a paradigmatic shift in practices from the use of task-specific architectures to the fine-tuning of pre-trained language models. The ongoing trend consists in training models with an ever-increasing amount of data and parameters, which requires considerable resources.

arxiv-2210-11652.title: Motion Primitives Based Kinodynamic RRT for Autonomous Vehicle Navigation in Complex Environments
arxiv-2210-11652.creator: Shubham Kedia, Sambhu H. Karumanchi
arxiv-2210-11652.description: Abstract In this work, we have implemented a SLAM-assisted navigation module for a real autonomous vehicle with unknown dynamics. The navigation objective is to reach a desired goal configuration along a collision-free trajectory while adhering to the dynamics of the system.

arxiv-2302-03105.title: Over 500 Days in the Life of the Photosphere of the Type Iax Supernova SN 2014dt TARDIS ( Kerzendorf & Sim 2014 ; Kerzendorf et al. 2023 ) , Jupyter ( Kluyver et al. 2016 ) , Astropy ( Astropy Collaboration et al. 2013 ; Astropy Collaboration et al. 2018 ) , IRAF ( Tody 1986 ; Tody 1993 ) , Matplotl
arxiv-2302-03105.creator: Yssavo Camacho-Neves, Saurabh W. Jha, Barnabas Barna, Mi Dai, Alexei V. Filippenko, Ryan J. Foley, Griffin Hosseinzadeh, D. Andrew Howell, Joel Johansson, Patrick L. Kelly, Wolfgang E. Kerzendorf, Lindsey A. Kwok, Conor Larison, Mark R. Magee, Curtis McCully, John T. O’Brien, Yen-Chen Pan, Viraj Pan
arxiv-2302-03105.description: Abstract Type Iax supernovae (SN Iax) are the largest known class of peculiar white dwarf supernovae, distinct from normal Type Ia supernovae (SN Ia). The unique properties of SN Iax, especially their strong photospheric lines out to extremely late times, allow us to model their optical spectra and derive physical parameters for the long-lasting photosphere.

arxiv-2411-16500.title: Cosmic structure formation in the non-linear regime Beyond Gaussian Statistics and Standard Cosmologies
arxiv-2411-16500.creator: Alexander Gough
arxiv-2411-16500.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Alexander Gough. The cosmic large scale structure encodes the formation and evolution of a weblike network of dark matter and galaxies within the Universe. The cosmological information is wrapped up in non-Gaussian statistics requiring characterisation beyond two-point correlations. Accurate modelling of these non-Gaussian statistics and the underlying non-linear dynamics of gravitational collapse are key to extracting maximal information from ongoing and upcoming cosmological surveys. This thesis centres on questions relating to clustering statistics, dynamics, and fundamental physics: A.

arxiv-2506-04700.title: Explicit Density Approximation for Neural Implicit Samplers Using a Bernstein-Based Convex Divergence
arxiv-2506-04700.creator: José Manuel de Frutos, Manuel A. Vázquez, Pablo M. Olmos, Joaquín Míguez
arxiv-2506-04700.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by José Manuel de Frutos, Manuel A. Vázquez, Pablo M. Olmos, Joaquín Míguez. Rank-based statistical metrics, such as the invariant statistical loss (ISL), have recently emerged as robust and practically effective tools for training implicit generative models. In this work, we introduce dual-ISL, a novel likelihood-free objective for training implicit generative models that interchanges the roles of the target and model distributions in the ISL framework, yielding a convex optimization problem in the space of model densities.

arxiv-2508-14941.title: Robust Symbolic Reasoning for Visual Narratives via Hierarchical and Semantically Normalized Knowledge Graphs
arxiv-2508-14941.creator: Yi-Chun Chen
arxiv-2508-14941.description: Abstract Understanding visual narratives such as comics requires structured representations that capture events, characters, and their relations across multiple levels of story organization. However, symbolic narrative graphs often suffer from inconsistency and redundancy, where similar actions or events are labeled differently across annotations or contexts. Such variance limits the effectiveness of reasoning and generalization.

pmc-13051830.title: Clinical Scores for Predicting Outcomes in Pediatric Oncology Sepsis: A Systematic Review and Meta‐Analysis
pmc-13051830.creator: Jesús Ángel Domínguez-Rojas, Silvio Torres, Alejandra Méndez Aceituno, Anita Arias, Gabriela Sequeria, Daniel Tatay, Lupe Mora Robles, Clotilde Mireya Muñoz, Luis Llano, Thomas Spentzas
pmc-13051830.description: BackgroundPediatric oncology patients with sepsis are at high risk of morbidity and mortality due to immunosuppression and acute or fulminant multiorgan dysfunction. pmc-13246753.title: MARCH2 prevents doxorubicin-induced cardiomyopathy by stabilizing NR1H2 and promoting clearance of apoptotic cardiomyocytes
pmc-13246753.creator: Shuolin Liu, Yiran E. Li, TingFang Zhu, LaiHai Zhang, Cong Yang, YaGuang Bi, Chenglong Bao, Ronggui Hu, Junbo Ge, Yingmei Zhang
pmc-13246753.description: Doxorubicin-induced cardiomyopathy (DiCM) involves impaired clearance of apoptotic cardiomyocytes (efferocytosis) by cardiac macrophages. This study reveals a central role for the MARCH2-NR1H2 axis in this process. We find that MARCH2 expression is significantly reduced in cardiac macrophages from DiCM mice and human dilated cardiomyopathy patients.

pmc-13261435.title: Spouted Bed Drying of Fresh Papaya Seeds (Carica papaya L.): Hydrodynamic Behavior and Statistical Analysis
pmc-13261435.creator: Alcino Matos de Azevedo Pontes Neto, Dhessyca Maria Vitoria Gonçalves Soares, Marlice Cruz Martelli, Davi do Socorro Barros Brasil
pmc-13261435.description: The processing of papaya (Carica papaya L.) generates substantial volumes of bioactive-rich seed residues that require efficient drying to prevent degradation. However, the hydrodynamic behavior of fresh seeds, characterized by high surface moisture and mucilaginous adhesion, remains poorly documented under spouted bed conditions. This study systematically investigated the drying performance of papaya seeds using a Box–Behnken experimental design.
